audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for judging, measure, speck/log, holy/pearls, ask-seek-knock, golden rule, narrow gate, false prophets, fruit discernment, Lord/Lord warning, doing the Father's will, rock/sand houses, authority response.

verses.restored: Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.

familiar.text: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

modern.text: “Do not judge, or you will be judged.

original.text: Μὴ κρίνετε, ἵνα μὴ κριθῆτε·

verses.restored: For with the judgment by which you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure by which you measure, it will be measured to you.

familiar.text: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.

modern.text: For with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged; and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.

original.text: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίματι κρίνετε κριθήσεσθε, καὶ ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: Why do you look at the speck in your brother's or sister's eye, but do not notice the beam in your own eye?

familiar.text: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

modern.text: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

original.text: τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ ἐν τῷ σῷ ὀφθαλμῷ δοκὸν οὐ κατανοεῖς;

verses.restored: Or how will you say to your brother or sister, Let me take the speck out of your eye, and look, the beam is in your own eye?

familiar.text: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye?

modern.text: How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while there is still a beam in your own eye?

original.text: ἢ πῶς ἐρεῖς τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος ⸀ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἡ δοκὸς ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ;

verses.restored: Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's or sister's eye.

familiar.text: Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.

modern.text: You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

original.text: ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ⸂ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ τὴν δοκόν⸃, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.

verses.restored: Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not throw your pearls before pigs, lest they trample them with their feet and turn and tear you.

familiar.text: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.

modern.text: Do not give dogs what is holy; do not throw your pearls before swine. If you do, they may trample them under their feet, and then turn and tear you to pieces. Ask, Seek, Knock (Luke 11:5–13)

original.text: Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἅγιον τοῖς κυσίν, μηδὲ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων, μήποτε ⸀καταπατήσουσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτῶν καὶ στραφέντες ῥήξωσιν ὑμᾶς.

verses.restored: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.

familiar.text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

modern.text: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.

original.text: Αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: For everyone who asks receives, the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.

familiar.text: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

modern.text: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.

original.text: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ⸀ἀνοιγήσεται.

verses.restored: Or what person among you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?

familiar.text: Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone?

modern.text: Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?

original.text: ἢ τίς ⸀ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος, ὃν ⸀αἰτήσει ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἄρτον— μὴ λίθον ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;

verses.restored: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a serpent?

familiar.text: Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent?

modern.text: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?

original.text: ⸀ἢ καὶ ⸂ἰχθὺν αἰτήσει⸃— μὴ ὄφιν ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ;

verses.restored: If you then, being harmful/mixed, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in the heavens give good things to those who ask him?

familiar.text: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

modern.text: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!

original.text: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὄντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς δώσει ἀγαθὰ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Therefore all things, whatever you want people to do to you, so also do to them; for this is the Law and the Prophets.

familiar.text: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

modern.text: In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets. The Narrow Gate (Luke 13:22–30)

original.text: Πάντα οὖν ὅσα ⸀ἐὰν θέλητε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς· οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται.

verses.restored: Enter through the narrow gate, because wide is the gate and spacious is the way leading into destruction, and many are those entering through it.

familiar.text: Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:

modern.text: Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.

original.text: Εἰσέλθατε διὰ τῆς στενῆς πύλης· ὅτι πλατεῖα ⸂ἡ πύλη⸃ καὶ εὐρύχωρος ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ἀπώλειαν, καὶ πολλοί εἰσιν οἱ εἰσερχόμενοι διʼ αὐτῆς·

verses.restored: How narrow the gate and compressed the way leading into life, and few are those finding it.

familiar.text: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.

modern.text: But small is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life, and only a few find it. A Tree and Its Fruit (Luke 6:43–45)

original.text: ⸀ὅτι στενὴ ἡ πύλη καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἀπάγουσα εἰς τὴν ζωήν, καὶ ὀλίγοι εἰσὶν οἱ εὑρίσκοντες αὐτήν.

verses.restored: Pay attention to false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves.

familiar.text: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

modern.text: Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.

original.text: ⸀Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν ψευδοπροφητῶν, οἵτινες ἔρχονται πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ἐνδύμασι προβάτων ἔσωθεν δέ εἰσιν λύκοι ἅρπαγες.

verses.restored: From their fruits you will recognize them. Do people gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?

familiar.text: Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

modern.text: By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

original.text: ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς. μήτι συλλέγουσιν ἀπὸ ἀκανθῶν ⸀σταφυλὰς ἢ ἀπὸ τριβόλων σῦκα;

verses.restored: In the same way, every good tree makes beautiful/good fruit, but the rotten tree makes harmful fruit.

familiar.text: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.

modern.text: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.

original.text: οὕτως πᾶν δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖ, τὸ δὲ σαπρὸν δένδρον καρποὺς πονηροὺς ποιεῖ·

verses.restored: A good tree is not able to make harmful fruit, nor a rotten tree to make beautiful/good fruit.

familiar.text: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

modern.text: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.

original.text: οὐ δύναται δένδρον ἀγαθὸν καρποὺς πονηροὺς ⸀ποιεῖν, οὐδὲ δένδρον σαπρὸν καρποὺς καλοὺς ποιεῖν.

verses.restored: Every tree not making beautiful/good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.

familiar.text: Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

modern.text: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

original.text: πᾶν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.

verses.restored: So then, from their fruits you will recognize them.

familiar.text: Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.

modern.text: So then, by their fruit you will recognize them.

original.text: ἄρα γε ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν αὐτῶν ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτούς.

verses.restored: Not everyone saying to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the reign of the heavens, but the one doing the will of my Father in the heavens.

familiar.text: Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.

modern.text: Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.

original.text: Οὐ πᾶς ὁ λέγων μοι· Κύριε κύριε εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἀλλʼ ὁ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν ⸀τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.

verses.restored: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, cast out unclean spirits in your name, and do many powers in your name?

familiar.text: Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?

modern.text: Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name drive out demons and perform many miracles?’

original.text: πολλοὶ ἐροῦσίν μοι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ· Κύριε κύριε, οὐ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι ἐπροφητεύσαμεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δαιμόνια ἐξεβάλομεν, καὶ τῷ σῷ ὀνόματι δυνάμεις πολλὰς ἐποιήσαμεν;

verses.restored: Then I will confess to them: I never knew you. Depart from me, workers of lawlessness.

familiar.text: And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.

modern.text: Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness!’ The House on the Rock (Luke 6:46–49)

original.text: καὶ τότε ὁμολογήσω αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐδέποτε ἔγνων ὑμᾶς· ἀποχωρεῖτε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ οἱ ἐργαζόμενοι τὴν ἀνομίαν.

verses.restored: Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

familiar.text: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:

modern.text: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

original.text: Πᾶς οὖν ὅστις ἀκούει μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ ποιεῖ αὐτούς, ⸀ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ φρονίμῳ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν ⸂αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν⸃ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.

verses.restored: The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house; but it did not fall, for it had been founded on the rock.

familiar.text: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

modern.text: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.

original.text: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέπεσαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἔπεσεν, τεθεμελίωτο γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν.

verses.restored: Everyone hearing these words of mine and not doing them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.

familiar.text: And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand:

modern.text: But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.

original.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀκούων μου τοὺς λόγους τούτους καὶ μὴ ποιῶν αὐτοὺς ὁμοιωθήσεται ἀνδρὶ μωρῷ, ὅστις ᾠκοδόμησεν ⸂αὐτοῦ τὴν οἰκίαν⸃ ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον.

verses.restored: The rain came down, the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house; and it fell, and its fall was great.

familiar.text: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it.

modern.text: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell—and great was its collapse!” The Authority of Jesus

original.text: καὶ κατέβη ἡ βροχὴ καὶ ἦλθον οἱ ποταμοὶ καὶ ἔπνευσαν οἱ ἄνεμοι καὶ προσέκοψαν τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἔπεσεν, καὶ ἦν ἡ πτῶσις αὐτῆς μεγάλη.

verses.restored: When Jesus finished these words, the crowds were astonished at his teaching.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Jesus had ended these sayings, the people were astonished at his doctrine:

modern.text: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were astonished at His teaching,

original.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ⸀ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ἐξεπλήσσοντο οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: For he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.

familiar.text: For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.

modern.text: because He taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes.

original.text: ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς ⸀αὐτῶν.
